parts.title: Definitions, Axioms, and Propositions on Substance and God

sentences: Something is **self-caused** if its essence involves **existence**.
A thing is **finite** if another thing of the **same nature** can limit it.
A **body** is finite because a greater body can be imagined, and a **thought** is limited by another thought.
A body is **not limited by thought**, nor is a thought by a body.
A **substance** exists and is conceived **in itself**.
An **attribute** is what the intellect perceives as constituting the **essence of substance**.
A **mode** is a modification of substance, existing and conceived through **something else**.
God is an **absolutely infinite being**, a substance with infinite attributes, each expressing **eternal and infinite essentiality**.
An **absolutely infinite** being contains all reality and involves **no negation**.
A thing is **free** if its existence and action are determined solely by its **own nature**.
A thing is **necessary or constrained** if determined by **something external**.
**Eternity** is existence necessarily following from the **definition of the eternal**, representing an **eternal truth**.
Everything exists **either in itself or in something else**.
What cannot be conceived through something else **must be conceived through itself**.
An **effect necessarily follows** from a definite cause, and its **knowledge involves the knowledge of its cause**.
Things with **nothing in common** cannot be understood by means of each other.
A **true idea** corresponds with its object.
If a thing can be conceived as **non-existing**, its essence does not involve existence.
**Substance is prior to its modifications**, and two substances with **different attributes** have nothing in common.
There cannot be **two or more substances of the same nature** or attribute in the universe.
A substance cannot be produced by **anything external** to itself.
The **existence of substance** is part of its nature, meaning its essence necessarily involves existence.
Every substance is **necessarily infinite** and **indivisible**.

parts.title: The Nature of Substance and God's Attributes

sentences: No **substance**, including extended substance, is **divisible**.
A part of substance is **finite substance**, which is a **contradiction** because the nature of substance is **infinite**.
Only **God** can be **granted** or **conceived** as substance, as God is an **absolutely infinite** being with every attribute of substance.
If another substance existed, it would share an attribute with God, which is **absurd**.
Therefore, **God is one**, the only substance, and this substance is **absolutely infinite**.
Both **extension and thought** are either **attributes of God** or **accidents** of his attributes.
All things **exist within God**, and nothing can exist or be conceived without him.
Modes must be in and conceived through the **divine nature**.
This means **everything is in God**.
Some people mistakenly believe God has a body, but divine nature denies this.
They think corporeal substance is separate from God, which shows they **do not understand their own words**.
No substance besides God can be granted or conceived.
Therefore, **extended substance is one of God's infinite attributes**.
Opponents argue that extended substance, being composed of parts, cannot be **infinite** or belong to God.
They suggest absurdities arise from dividing infinite extended substance, like an infinite being composed of **finite parts**.
They also claim that God cannot be **passive**, but divisible extended substance is passive.
These arguments are based on the **absurd hypothesis** that extended substance is composed of parts.
Infinite quantity is **not measurable** and **cannot be composed of finite parts**.
Dividing quantity is a human tendency when viewed through **imagination**, making it seem finite and divisible.
When quantity is understood as **substance** through the intellect, it is **infinite, one, and indivisible**.
Matter's parts are only distinguishable **modally**, not really.
Water, as **extended substance**, is neither separated nor divisible.
God is the **efficient cause** of all things, and individual things are **modifications of God's attributes**.
God acts solely by the **laws of his own nature**, making him the **sole free cause**.
God and all his attributes are **eternal**.
God's intellect and will are the **cause of things' essence and existence**.

parts.title: Divine Conditioning and the Nature of Existence

sentences: A thing **conditioned by God** cannot become unconditioned.
Everything **finite** and with a **conditioned existence** needs another finite cause, and this chain extends **infinitely**.
Finite things come from God's attributes only when those attributes are **modified** by a **finite, conditioned modification**.
This modification is also **conditioned by another finite cause**, and so on, **infinitely**.
God is the **immediate cause** of things produced directly by his **absolute nature**.
Nothing in the universe is **contingent**; everything is **conditioned** by the **necessity of the divine nature**.
Nature viewed as **active (natura naturans)** represents God as a **free cause**.
Nature viewed as **passive (natura naturata)** includes all that follows from the **necessity of God's nature**.
Intellect, will, and desire are modes of thinking and belong to **passive nature**, not active nature.
Will is not a **free cause** but a **necessary cause**, requiring a **conditioning cause**.
God does not act according to **freedom of the will**.
Things could not have been created by God in **any other manner or order** than they are.

parts.title: Imagination, Perception, and the Nature of Mind

sentences: People judge things based on their **brain's state** or, more accurately, mistake the **forms of their imagination** for actual things.
This leads to disagreements where one person's **"good"** is another's **"bad"**, or one's **"orderly"** is another's **"confused"**.
These differing perceptions explain the rise of **controversies and skepticism**.
Common sayings like "So many men, so many minds" illustrate that people **imagine** more than they **understand**.
If people truly **understood phenomena**, they would be convinced by mathematical reasoning.
All common explanations of nature are merely **modes of imagining** and do not reveal the **true nature of anything**.
These imaginary entities, despite having names, are **not real**.
Arguments about **imperfections in nature**, such as decay or evil, are easily refuted.
The **perfection of things** is judged by their own nature and power, not by how they affect human senses or serve humanity.
God's nature is so **vast** that it can produce everything conceivable by an **infinite intelligence**.
The author undertakes to note these **misconceptions** and believes they can be dissipated with reflection.
The discussion then moves to the **nature and origin of the mind**, explaining concepts that stem from the **essence of God**.

Key terms are defined: **Body** is a mode expressing God's essence as an extended thing, and something belongs to a thing's essence if its presence or absence **necessarily implies** the thing's presence or absence.
An **idea** is a mental conception, distinct from perception as it implies **activity of the mind**.
An **adequate idea** possesses all the intrinsic marks of a true idea, excluding external agreement with an object.

parts.title: The Human Mind and Body: Union and Nature

sentences: The **human mind**'s object is the **body**, specifically a **mode of extension** that truly exists.
If the body were not the mind's object, ideas of **bodily modifications** would not be in **God** as he constitutes our mind.
We **do** possess ideas of bodily modifications.
The mind's object is the **actually existing body** and nothing else.
To understand the mind fully, you need **adequate knowledge of the body's nature**.
An idea of **everything** exists in God, like the human body's idea.
To understand how the **human mind** differs, its object's nature, the **human body**, must be known.
A body fit for many actions makes its **mind** fitted for many **simultaneous perceptions**.
If a body's actions depend more on itself, its mind is more capable of **distinct comprehension**.
Bodies are distinguished by **motion, rest, quickness, and slowness**, not **substance**.
A body in motion stays in motion until another body makes it rest.
Bodies are in **union** when compelled to remain in contact or move with a **fixed mutual relation**, forming one individual body.
If parts of a composite body are replaced by equal parts of the same nature, the individual **preserves its nature**.
The **human mind** does not have **adequate knowledge** of the **human body**.
The **idea of each modification** of the human body does not provide **adequate knowledge** of an **external body**, as such knowledge resides in **God**.
The **human mind perceives external bodies** only through the **ideas of its body's modifications**.
When the **mind imagines** an external body, it **lacks adequate knowledge** of it.
The **idea of a modification** of the human body does not offer **adequate knowledge** of the **human body itself**.
Ideas of human body modifications, when referred only to the **human mind**, are **confused**, not **clear and distinct**.
The **idea of the idea** of each body modification does not imply **adequate knowledge** of the **human mind**.
The **human mind** only has **confused and fragmentary knowledge** of itself, its body, and external bodies when it perceives things in the **common order of nature**.
This occurs when the mind is **determined from without** by circumstances, not **from within** by understanding multiple things at once.
The **duration of our body** and other **particular things** can only be known **very inadequately**.
This means all **particular things are contingent and perishable**.
All **ideas in God are true**.
There is **nothing positive in ideas that makes them false**.
Falsity is the **privation of knowledge** found in **inadequate, fragmentary, or confused ideas**.
**Inadequate and confused ideas** follow with the **same necessity** as **adequate ones**.
Things **common to all bodies**, and equally present in parts and the whole, do not form the **essence of any particular thing**.
These **common things** can only be conceived **adequately**.

parts.title: Reason, God's Essence, and the Nature of Will

sentences: Reason perceives things as **necessary**, not **contingent**.
This **necessity** is the **eternal nature of God**.
Therefore, reason views things under a **form of eternity**.
The bases of reason are **notions** common to all things, conceived **without relation to time**.
Every idea of an existing particular thing necessarily involves the **eternal and infinite essence of God**.
Particular things cannot be conceived without **God**.
Their ideas involve the **conception of God's attributes**, which is His **eternal and infinite essence**.
Existence here does not mean duration but the **very nature of existence**.
This nature is assigned to things because they follow from the **eternal necessity of God's nature**.
The force by which each particular thing perseveres in existing follows from **God's eternal necessity**.
The knowledge of **God's eternal and infinite essence** that every idea involves is **adequate and perfect**.
This knowledge is common to all, equally in the part and in the whole, thus making it **adequate**.
The **human mind** has an **adequate knowledge** of **God's eternal and infinite essence**.
This is derived from its ideas of itself, its body, and external bodies.
The **infinite essence** and **eternity of God** are known to all.
Many things can be adequately known from this knowledge, leading to a **third kind of knowledge**.
Men have a less clear knowledge of God than of general notions because they cannot **imagine God as bodies**.
They associate God's name with **images of things they see**, leading to errors.
Errors arise from not applying **names to things rightly** or misinterpreting meanings.
The mind has **no absolute or free will**.
The mind is determined to wish by a cause, which is determined by another cause, extending to **infinity**.
There is **no absolute faculty of understanding, desiring, loving** in the mind.
These faculties are abstract terms from particular things.
The will to affirm and decide is a **faculty**, not a desire.
It is the faculty by which the mind affirms or denies what is true or false.

parts.title: Mind and Body: Activity, Passivity, and Interplay

sentences: A mind with **adequate ideas** is **active**.
A mind with **inadequate ideas** is **passive**.
The **mind's activity** depends on its **adequate ideas**.
The **mind's passivity** depends on its **inadequate ideas**.
The **body cannot make the mind think**.
The **mind cannot make the body move**.
All **thinking** comes from **God** as a **thinking thing**.
What influences the mind is a **mode of thought**, not the **body**.
All **body motion** comes from **another body**.
Everything in a body comes from **God** as an **extended mode**.
It **cannot originate from the mind**.
Mind and body are **one thing** with two attributes: **thought** and **extension**.
Their **activity and passivity** are the **same**.
People often believe the **mind controls the body**.
However, no one knows the **limits of the body's power** by **natural laws alone**.
**Animals** and **somnambulists** show the body can do **many wonders** without the mind.
People mistakenly credit the mind for physical actions when they **don't know the true cause**.
If the **mind is unfit for thinking**, the **body is inert**.
If the **body is inactive**, the **mind is unfit for thinking**.
The **mind's fitness** changes with the **body's fitness** to be stimulated.
People believe they are free because they are **conscious of actions** but **unconscious of their causes**.
Mental decisions are **appetites** that change with the **body's state**.
A **mental decision** and a **bodily appetite** are the **same thing**, seen differently.

parts.title: Emotions of Love, Hate, and Their Effects

sentences: If you imagine that the object of your **love is destroyed**, you will feel **pain**.
Conversely, if you imagine it is **preserved**, you will feel **pleasure**.
When you imagine that the object of your **hate is destroyed**, you will feel **pleasure**.
If you conceive that the object of your **love** experiences **pleasure or pain**, you will feel that same **pleasure or pain** yourself.
This emotional response is **greater or lesser** depending on the intensity of the emotion in the loved object.
If something brings **pleasure** to an object of your love, you will feel **love towards that thing**.
If it brings **pain**, you will feel **hatred**.
Pity is defined as **pain arising from another's hurt**.
Approval is the **love** felt towards someone who benefits another, and **indignation** is the **hatred** for someone who harms another.
You feel **pity** not only for loved things but also for things resembling yourself, even if previously unregarded.
If you imagine an object of your **hatred is painfully affected**, you will feel **pleasure**.
If it is **pleasurably affected**, you will feel **pain**.
These emotions vary with the intensity of the opposite emotion in the hated object.
Hatred, especially envy, makes a person **rejoice in another's hurt** and **grieve at their advantage**.
We strive to **affirm** things that bring us or our loved ones **pleasure** and to **negative** things that cause **pain**.
We also try to **affirm** things that bring **pain** to what we hate and **deny** what brings it **pleasure**.
It is possible to **overestimate** oneself or a loved one, or **underestimate** a hated object.
Pride is **pleasure** from thinking too highly of oneself, a kind of **madness** where one believes they can achieve anything they conceive.
Over-esteem is **pleasure** from thinking too highly of another, while disdain is **pleasure** from thinking too little of another.
A man who **conceives** someone has **injured** him out of **hatred** will seek **retaliation**.
He will then **hate** his enemy and try to **injure** them.
The **endeavor** to injure someone hated is **Anger**, and to repay injury is **Revenge**.
Believing one is loved without cause leads to reciprocal **love**.
Reciprocal **love** and desire to **benefit** the lover is **gratitude**.
Men often seek **vengeance** more than returning **benefits**.
If **hatred** is stronger than love for someone who loves you, one tries to injure them; this is **cruelty**.
Giving a benefit from **love** or **honor** causes **pain** if received without **gratitude**.
**Hatred** increases when reciprocated but can be destroyed by **love**.
**Hatred** overcome by **love** transforms into greater **love**.
Joy from destroying something hated comes with some **pain** from seeing something similar to oneself suffer.
**Love** or **hatred** is greater for a free entity, seen as the sole cause.
People feel more **love** or **hatred** towards each other, believing they are **free**.
**Repentance** is **pain** with oneself as the cause, while **self-complacency** is **pleasure** with oneself as the cause.
**Wonder** is imagining a unique thing; if by fear, it's **Consternation**; if by love, it's **Devotion**.
**Contempt** denies qualities that cause wonder, love, or fear.
**Derision** comes from contempt for a hated or feared thing, **Scorn** from contempt of folly.
The mind feels **pleasure** regarding its activity, especially when praised by others.
It feels **pain** contemplating its weakness, fostered if blamed by others.
This pain is **humility**, and pleasure from self-contemplation is **self-love**.
Men are naturally **envious**, rejoicing in equals' shortcomings and pained by their virtues.
No one envies a non-**equal**.
Many kinds of **pleasure**, **pain**, and **desire** exist, reflecting diverse objects.
All emotions relate to **desire**, **pleasure**, or **pain**.
**Desire** is an individual's nature.
**Pleasure** and **pain** are passive states that change one's power to persist.
**Pleasure** and **desire** are also attributable when we are **active**.
Actions from emotions attributed to the understanding mind are **strength of character**, including **courage** and **highmindedness**.

parts.title: The Nature and Definitions of Emotions

sentences: The **emotions** can be **compounded** in many ways, leading to **numerous variations** that are beyond calculation.
Only the **most important** emotions are listed, as enumerating all variations would be more **curious than profitable**.
When enjoying something longed for, the body acquires a **new disposition**, which changes how the mind conceives and desires.
For example, enjoying food fills the stomach, causing the body to dispose of it differently.
This **new disposition** can lead to **repugnance** for the food previously desired, a feeling called **satiety or weariness**.
**Desire** is defined as the **actual essence of man**, determined by a **modification of itself** for a particular activity.
This definition encompasses **appetite, will, desire, or impulse**, which vary by individual disposition.
**Pleasure** is the **transition** from a lesser to a **greater perfection**, and **pain** is the transition from a greater to a **lesser perfection**.
Perfection itself is not pleasure; if one were born with perfect contentment, the emotion of pleasure would not exist.
Pain is not merely the absence of greater perfection, but an **activity of transition** that **lessens or constrains** one's power of action.
**Wonder** is the mind's conception of something that causes it to **pause**, as the concept has **no connection** to other existing concepts.
The mind will remain fixated on the **new image** until other factors prompt it to consider something else.

parts.title: Human Bondage and the Nature of Perfection, Good, and Evil

sentences: Human infirmity in moderating emotions is called **bondage**.
A person becomes a **prey to emotions** and not their own master.
They often follow what is **worse**, even when seeing what is better.
This happens because **perfection and imperfection**, and **good and evil** are misunderstood.
A work is **perfect** if it reaches its author's **intention and aim**.
If the author's aim is unknown, the work cannot be judged.
Men form **general ideas** and call **perfect** what aligns with their type.
Natural phenomena are also judged based on these human **general ideas**.
People believe Nature has these types in view, and if something does not conform, they say Nature has **blundered** or left work **incomplete**.
Nature does not work with an **end in view**.
God or Nature acts by the same **necessity** as that by which it exists.
A **final cause** is merely **human desire** considered as the origin of something.
Men are **ignorant** of the causes determining their desires.
Claims about Nature's imperfections are based on **prejudices**, not true knowledge.
**Perfection and imperfection** are actually **modes of thinking**, comparing individuals of the same species.
**Reality and perfection** mean the same thing, referring all individual things to the category of **Being**.
Things with more **being or reality** are considered more **perfect**.
**Good and bad** are also **modes of thinking**, not positive qualities in things themselves.
A man passes from lesser to greater **perfection** when his **power of action** is increased.

parts.title: The Nature of Virtue and Self-Preservation

sentences: Every person, by their nature, **desires** what is useful and **avoids** what is harmful.
The more someone tries to **preserve their being**, the more **virtuous** they are.
Virtue is **human power**, defined by the effort to **persist** in one's own being.
No one neglects their good unless **external causes** overcome them.
People do not naturally shrink from food or kill themselves unless **compelled** by outside forces.
Such compulsion can be direct force, escaping a **greater evil**, or external causes **disordering** imagination and body.
It is impossible for a person to naturally seek non-existence.
No one desires **blessedness** or to **act rightly** without also wishing to **exist**.
The desire for right living is the **essence of man**, which is the **endeavor to preserve being**.
No virtue can exist **prior** to the effort of **self-preservation**.
This effort is the **first and only foundation of virtue**.
Acting from **inadequate ideas** is not acting virtuously; acting from **understanding** is.
To act virtuously means to act in accordance with **reason** and **self-interest**.
No one wishes to preserve their being for **anything else's sake**.
What we endeavor to do in obedience to reason is to **understand**.
The mind considers useful only what **conduces to understanding**.
We only know things as good or evil if they **promote or hinder understanding**.
The mind's highest good and virtue is the **knowledge of God**.
Thinking only of **gain** or **money** is not seen as madness, because these people are often **harmful** and seen as worthy of **hatred**.
However, **Avarice**, **Ambition**, and **Lust** are types of **madness**, even if not called diseases.
Hatred is **never** good; hating someone means trying to **destroy** them, which is a **bad** act.
Envy, derision, contempt, anger, and revenge, which come from hatred, are also **bad**.
Any desire driven by hatred is **base** and **unjust** in a State.
Laughter and joking are forms of **pleasure** and are **good** if not too much.
People should enjoy themselves with **moderate** and **pleasant** food, drink, perfumes, plants, clothes, music, sports, and theaters, without harming others.
The body needs **varied nourishment** for all parts to work well, helping the mind understand many things at **once**.
A person using **reason** will try to give **love** or **kindness** for hatred, anger, or contempt, because hatred grows when returned but can end with love.
Those who try to **conquer hatred with love** fight with joy and confidence.
Hope and fear are not good because they need **pain** to exist.
These feelings show **defective knowledge** and weak mental power.
More reason means less dependence on hope and fear, aiming to control **fortune** with wisdom.
Over-esteem and disparagement are always **bad** feelings because they go against reason.
Pity is **bad** and **useless** for someone led by reason, as it is a pain; actions to help should come from reason, not emotion.
Understanding **nature's necessity** means not feeling hatred, derision, contempt, or pity.
Approval aligns with reason, coming from **love** for good deeds.
Self-approval, especially from **reason** and seeing one's true power, is the **highest** goal.
Humility and repentance are not virtues; they are forms of **pain** or **infirmity**.
For those without reason, humility, repentance, hope, and fear can be helpful, stopping worse acts and possibly leading to **reason**.

parts.title: Notes on Goodwill, Ingratitude, Freedom, and Reason

sentences: Goodwill among men driven by **blind desire** is often a **bargaining** or **enticement**, not pure goodwill.
Ingratitude is not an emotion but is **base** as it shows **excessive hatred, anger, pride, or avarice**.
A person who does not know how to return benefits due to **folly** is not ungrateful.
Similarly, one who is not swayed by a courtesan's gifts or a thief's bribes shows a **constant mind**.
Such a person cannot be corrupted to their own or the **general hurt**.
The **free man** never acts **fraudulently**, but always in **good faith**.
If breaking faith would save a man from **present death**, his plan of **self-preservation** might persuade him to deceive.
However, if reason persuaded him to act thus, it would persuade all men to do so.
This would mean reason would persuade men not to **agree in good faith** to unite forces or have **common laws**, which is **absurd**.
A man guided by **reason** is **more free** in a **State** with a general system of law than in **solitude**.
Such a man does not obey through **fear**.
He desires to order his life according to the **general good** and the **laws of his country**.
Therefore, to enjoy greater freedom, the **free man** desires **general rights of citizenship**.
These observations on true freedom relate to **strength**, specifically **courage** and **nobility of character**.
A strong person **hates no man**, is **angry with no man**, **envies no man**, is **indignant with no man**, **despises no man**, and is least of all **proud**.
These points are proven by overcoming **hatred with love** and desiring for others the good one seeks for oneself.
The strong man recognizes that all things follow from the **necessity of the divine nature**.
What seems **hurtful, evil, impious, horrible, unjust, and base** appears so due to a **disordered, fragmentary, and confused view of the universe**.
He strives to conceive things as they truly are and remove hindrances to **true knowledge**, such as **hatred, anger, envy, derision, and pride**.
He endeavors to do good and go on his way **rejoicing**.

parts.title: The Power of the Mind Over Emotions and the Eternal Love of God

sentences: Those who **criticize** the misuse of **honor** often **desire** it most.
This is common in **unfortunate** and **spiritually weak** people.
A **miserly poor person** talks about the **vices of the rich**, showing **intolerance** of their **own poverty**.
Those rejected by a woman focus on **inconstancy**, but forget it when **accepted**.
Someone controlling emotions through **love of freedom** seeks **knowledge of virtues**.
This brings **joy** and prevents dwelling on **men's faults**.
Observing these precepts allows one to **direct actions** by **reason**.
A **mental image** referred to **more objects** is more frequent and vivid.
This is because more causes **arouse** it, and the mind **contemplates them simultaneously**.
Mental images are **easily associated** with things **clearly understood**.
Things **clearly understood** are common properties and are **often aroused**.
A **mental image** is more vivid when **associated with more other images**.
The **mind can refer** all **bodily modifications** to the **idea of God**.
One who **understands himself** and his **emotions loves God**, and this love **increases with understanding**.
This **love towards God** holds the **chief place in the mind** as it is fostered by **all bodily modifications**.
**God is without passions** and does not **love or hate anyone**.
No one can **hate God** because the idea of God is **adequate**, leading to **activity** and no pain.
This **love towards God** is constant and **cannot be destroyed** unless the **body is destroyed**.
The mind's power over emotions comes from **knowing them** and understanding them **distinctly**.
**Spiritual unhealthiness** comes from **excessive love** for **variable things**.
**Clear knowledge**, especially of God, influences emotions, making them occupy a **small part of the mind**.
This fosters **love towards an immutable and eternal thing**.
